facts.fact: Publishing an app via Cloudflare Tunnel requires a domain already added to Cloudflare; the server must reach Cloudflare on port 7844 (outbound).
cloudflared initiates an outbound connection from origin to Cloudflare; all inbound traffic can be blocked at the firewall. (Page did not mention CGNAT explicitly.)
hypotheses: Outbound-only implies it works behind CGNAT/dynamic IP; not stated on the page

facts.fact: Zero Trust account limits page: 1,000 cloudflared tunnels per account, 25 active replicas per tunnel, 500 Access applications default; Free accounts 50 custom Application Library apps. No free-plan seat figure on that page.

Free Zero Trust plan seat limit: search snippets say Cloudflare's pages state 'up to 50 users' on the Free plan (Access page: 'Try it forever for up to 50 users'). Official pages fetched directly did not state the number; only search-result snippets.
hypotheses: Free tier = 50 seats; verify on cloudflare.com/plans/zero-trust-services before relying

facts.fact: Caddy automatic HTTPS: needs A/AAAA DNS pointing to server and ports 80/443 reachable for HTTP/TLS-ALPN challenges; DNS challenge needs no open ports but needs DNS provider credentials; data dir must be persistent.
Cloudflare Origin CA certs only encrypt Cloudflare-to-origin traffic, are not browser-trusted, work with Full (strict) mode, and Cloudflare sends no expiry notifications; validity chosen at creation.

pg_dump can dump servers back to 9.2 but refuses a server newer than itself; dump output is expected to load into newer versions; loading into an older server is not guaranteed and may need manual editing.

pg_dump is a logical backup and cannot be used for continuous archiving/PITR; base backup + WAL archiving gives PITR, whole-cluster only; docs say continuous archiving is preferred where high reliability is needed; test archiving before first base backup and inspect data after recovery; unmonitored archive_command failure can fill pg_wal; config files are not captured.
pgBackRest supports full/differential/incremental backups, parallel async WAL push/get, retention policies, and ten PostgreSQL versions (five current plus last five EOL).
R2 free tier (Standard storage): 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A ops/month, 10 million Class B ops/month, egress free; not applicable to Infrequent Access.

github.com/minio/minio is AGPLv3 and its README says 'THIS REPOSITORY IS NO LONGER MAINTAINED'; archived 2026-04-25; community edition source-only, no new binaries; alternatives named are AIStor Free and AIStor Enterprise. Docs URL 301-redirects to docs.min.io/enterprise/aistor-object-store. MinIO resource needs not retrieved.

GlitchTip: needs PostgreSQL 14+, a GlitchTip service (all-in-one or web+worker), optional Valkey/Redis 7+; recommended 512 MB RAM, minimum 256 MB all-in-one; ~30 GB disk per ~1M events/month; sample compose.yml provided.
Uptime Kuma ships compose.yaml in repo; image louislam/uptime-kuma:2 on port 3001; can bind to 127.0.0.1; NFS storage unsupported; no RAM requirement listed on page.

Docker restart policies: no (default), on-failure[:n], always, unless-stopped; unless-stopped keeps manually stopped containers stopped across daemon restart/reboot; policy applies only after container has run 10 seconds.

PostgreSQL docs: fsync=off can cause unrecoverable corruption after power failure; full_page_writes=off risks corruption; synchronous_commit=off loses recent commits but not consistency (up to 3x wal_writer_delay window).
Docker published ports are diverted in the nat table before ufw rules apply, so ufw is effectively bypassed for published container ports.
Docker daemon runs as root unless rootless; only trusted users should control it; containers can mount host / without restriction. Page does not literally say 'socket access equals root'.
